cases.explain: Малый is the predicate noun describing он (he) after the implied verb 'to be', so it stands in the nominative case.

cases.sentence: Нехорошо, что ты не ездишь на собрание и вообще устранился от земского ___.
cases.translation: It's not good that you don't go to the assembly and have withdrawn from district affairs altogether.
cases.explain: The preposition от (from/away from) governs the genitive case.

cases.sentence: Константин Левин чувствовал себя нравственно припертым к ___.
cases.translation: Konstantin Levin felt morally backed into a corner.
cases.explain: The preposition к (against/toward) governs the dative case.

cases.translation: And Sergei Ivanovich put a dilemma to him.
cases.explain: Дилемму is the direct object of поставил (put/posed), so it takes the accusative case.

cases.translation: "Allow me," Sergei Ivanovich interrupted with a smile.
cases.explain: The preposition с (with) governs the instrumental case.

cases.sentence: Когда бы в ___ мне сказали, что другие понимают интегральное вычисление, а я не понимаю, тут самолюбие.
cases.translation: If I had been told at the university that others understand integral calculus and I don't, that would be a matter of pride.
cases.explain: The preposition в (in/at) governs the prepositional case.

cases.sentence: Для меня земские учреждения просто повинность платить 18 копеек с ___.
cases.translation: For me, the district institutions are simply an obligation to pay 18 kopecks per desyatina.
cases.explain: The preposition с (per/from) governs the genitive case here.

cases.sentence: Быть присяжным и судить мужика, укравшего ___.
cases.translation: To be a juror and judge a peasant who stole ham.
cases.explain: Ветчину is the direct object of укравшего (having stolen), so it takes the accusative case.

reading.ru: «А знаешь, я о тебе думал», — сказал Сергей Иванович.
reading.question: What did Sergei Ivanovich tell Konstantin he had been thinking about?
reading.correct: About him (Konstantin)
reading.explain: Sergei Ivanovich opened by saying he had been thinking about Konstantin.

reading.ru: И я тебе говорил и говорю.
reading.question: What does Sergei Ivanovich emphasize he has repeatedly told Konstantin?
options: His criticism about withdrawing from district (zemstvo) affairs
That he should sell the estate
reading.correct: His criticism about withdrawing from district (zemstvo) affairs
reading.explain: This follows his repeated criticism that Konstantin does not attend meetings and has withdrawn from zemstvo work.

reading.ru: Деньги мы платим, они идут на жалование, а нет ни школ, ни фельдшеров, ни повивальных бабок, ни аптек, ничего нет».
reading.question: What does Sergei Ivanovich complain about regarding the district's money?
options: That money is paid out in salaries but there are no schools, doctors' assistants, midwives, or pharmacies to show for it
That there is no money left at all
That the peasants refuse to pay any taxes
That the money is being stolen by officials
reading.correct: That money is paid out in salaries but there are no schools, doctors' assistants, midwives, or pharmacies to show for it
reading.explain: Sergei Ivanovich complains that the money collected goes to salaries while there are no schools, medical assistants, midwives, or pharmacies.

reading.ru: Я пробовал и вижу, что ничего не могу сделать», — сказал Левин.
reading.question: What does Levin say about his attempts to participate in district affairs?
options: That he tried and sees that he can accomplish nothing
That he never tried at all
That he plans to try again next year
reading.correct: That he tried and sees that he can accomplish nothing
reading.explain: Levin says he tried and sees that he can do nothing in this regard.

reading.ru: Ты сделал попытку и не удалось, по-твоему, и ты покоряешься.
reading.question: How does Sergei Ivanovich characterize Levin's response to his failed attempt?
options: That he made an attempt, it failed in his view, and he simply gives up
That he succeeded but claims otherwise
That he blamed others for the failure
reading.correct: That he made an attempt, it failed in his view, and he simply gives up
reading.explain: Sergei Ivanovich says Levin made an attempt, considered it a failure, and then simply submitted/gave up.

reading.ru: «Неужели уж отпахали?» — подумал он.
reading.question: What practical concern distracted Levin during the philosophical conversation?
options: Whether the plowing was already finished
Whether it was going to rain
Whether the doctor had left yet
reading.correct: Whether the plowing was already finished
reading.explain: Levin's mind wandered to whether the plowing had already been finished, showing his attention was on farm matters, not the debate.

reading.ru: И Сергей Иванович поставил ему дилемму.
reading.question: What did Sergei Ivanovich do to press his argument?
options: He posed a dilemma to Levin
He apologized and dropped the argument
He asked their mother to intervene
reading.correct: He posed a dilemma to Levin
reading.explain: Sergei Ivanovich confronted Levin with a dilemma to force him to justify his position.

reading.ru: Нельзя, хорошо разместив деньги, дать врачебную помощь?
reading.question: What rhetorical question does Sergei Ivanovich raise about medical aid?
options: Whether proper allocation of money could not provide medical assistance
Whether doctors are unnecessary in the countryside
Whether peasants refuse all medical treatment
Whether hospitals already exist in the district
reading.correct: Whether proper allocation of money could not provide medical assistance
reading.explain: Sergei Ivanovich asks whether, with money properly allocated, medical assistance couldn't be provided.

reading.ru: Константин Левин чувствовал себя нравственно припертым к стене и потому разгорячился и высказал невольно главную причину своего равнодушия к общему делу.
reading.question: How did Levin feel during the argument, prompting him to reveal his true reason for indifference?
options: Morally cornered, which made him grow heated and blurt out his real reason
reading.correct: Morally cornered, which made him grow heated and blurt out his real reason
reading.explain: Levin felt morally backed into a corner, which caused him to grow heated and reveal the real reason for his indifference.

reading.ru: Он помолчал, вынул одну удочку, перекинул и, улыбаясь, обратился к брату.
reading.question: What did Sergei Ivanovich do before responding with a new argument?
options: He paused, cast one of the fishing rods, and smilingly turned to his brother
He stood up angrily and walked away
He called for the doctor to settle the dispute
reading.correct: He paused, cast one of the fishing rods, and smilingly turned to his brother
reading.explain: Sergei Ivanovich paused, cast a fishing line, and then, smiling, turned to address his brother with a new argument.

reading.ru: Вот мы для Агафьи Михайловны послали заземским доктором.
reading.question: What example does Sergei Ivanovich use to argue for the value of medical points?
options: Sending for the district doctor for Agafya Mikhailovna
Building a new hospital in the village
Hiring a private nurse for the household
Sending Agafya Mikhailovna to the city
reading.correct: Sending for the district doctor for Agafya Mikhailovna
reading.explain: Sergei Ivanovich points out that they sent for the zemstvo (district) doctor for Agafya Mikhailovna as an example of a medical point's usefulness.

reading.ru: «Грамотный, как работник, гораздо хуже.
reading.question: What is Levin's counterargument about literate peasant workers?
options: That a literate worker is much worse as a laborer
That literacy makes workers more honest
That literate workers are paid less
That literacy has no effect either way
reading.correct: That a literate worker is much worse as a laborer
reading.explain: Levin argues that a literate worker is, as a laborer, much worse.

reading.ru: «Признаешь ли ты, что образование есть благо для народа?» «Признаю», — сказал Левин нечаянно и тотчас же подумал, что он сказал не то, что думает.
reading.question: How did Levin respond when asked if education is a good for the people?
options: He said yes, but immediately regretted it, feeling he hadn't said what he really thought
He asked to change the subject
reading.correct: He said yes, but immediately regretted it, feeling he hadn't said what he really thought
reading.explain: Levin answered 'I admit it' unintentionally, and immediately thought he had said something other than what he actually believed.

reading.ru: «Если ты признаешь это благом, — сказал Сергей Иванович, — то ты, как честный человек, не можешь не любить и не сочувствовать такому делу и потому не желать работать для него».
reading.question: What logical trap does Sergei Ivanovich set after Levin admits education is a good?
options: That as an honest man, Levin cannot help but love and want to work for such a cause
That Levin must now pay for all the schools himself
That Levin must apologize to the peasants
That Levin must resign from his estate duties
reading.correct: That as an honest man, Levin cannot help but love and want to work for such a cause
reading.explain: Sergei Ivanovich argues that if Levin admits education is good, as an honest man he must sympathize with and want to work for it.

reading.ru: «Вот к чему, — горячась заговорил он, — я думаю, что двигатель всех наших действий есть все-таки личное счастье.
reading.question: What does Levin argue is the true motivator of all human actions?
reading.correct: Personal happiness/self-interest
reading.explain: Levin argues, growing heated, that personal happiness is still the driving force behind all their actions.

reading.ru: Для меня земские учреждения просто повинность платить 18 копеек с десятины, ездить в город, ночевать с клопами и слушать всякий вздор и гадости, а личный интерес меня не побуждает».
reading.question: How does Levin describe his personal experience of zemstvo institutions?
options: As a burden of paying money, traveling to the city, sleeping with bedbugs, and listening to nonsense, with no personal interest driving him
As a source of pride and fulfillment
As something that benefits him financially
reading.correct: As a burden of paying money, traveling to the city, sleeping with bedbugs, and listening to nonsense, with no personal interest driving him
reading.explain: Levin describes zemstvo duties as an unwelcome obligation involving payments, travel, bedbugs, and nonsense, with no personal interest motivating him.

reading.ru: Хотелось сбросить с себя это ярмо, которое давило нас, всех хороших людей.
reading.question: How does Levin describe the motivation behind the emancipation of the serfs?
options: A desire to throw off a yoke that oppressed all good people, including himself
Pure altruism with no personal stake
reading.correct: A desire to throw off a yoke that oppressed all good people, including himself
reading.explain: Levin explains that they wanted to throw off the yoke that weighed on them, on all good people, showing personal interest was involved.

reading.ru: Но судить, куда распределить 40 тысяч земских денег или Алешку-дурачка судить, я не понимаю и не могу».
reading.question: What kind of civic duty does Levin say he cannot understand or perform?
options: Deciding how to allocate 40,000 zemstvo rubles or judging a simple peasant like Alyoshka
reading.correct: Deciding how to allocate 40,000 zemstvo rubles or judging a simple peasant like Alyoshka
reading.explain: Levin says he cannot understand or bring himself to judge how to distribute zemstvo funds or to judge a simpleton like Alyoshka.

reading.ru: «Наши учреждения и все это похоже на березки, которые мы натыкали, как в троицин день, для того, чтобы было похоже на лес, который сам вырос в Европе.
reading.question: What metaphor does Levin use to criticize Russian institutions modeled on Europe?
options: Birch branches stuck in the ground like decorations, imitating a forest that grew naturally in Europe
A house built without a foundation
reading.correct: Birch branches stuck in the ground like decorations, imitating a forest that grew naturally in Europe
reading.explain: Levin compares Russian institutions to birch branches stuck in the ground for a holiday, meant to look like the forest that actually grew naturally in Europe.

reading.ru: Это общая истина, философская, — сказал он, с решительностью повторяя слово «философская», как будто желая показать, что он тоже имеет право, как и всякий, говорить о философии».
reading.question: Why does Levin repeat the word 'philosophical' with determination?
options: To assert his right to discuss philosophy just like anyone else
Because he forgot what he was saying
Because his brother asked him to repeat it
Because he was quoting a book directly
reading.correct: To assert his right to discuss philosophy just like anyone else
reading.explain: Levin insists on the word 'philosophical' to show he too has the right to speak about philosophy, as anyone does.

reading.ru: «Ну уж об философии ты оставь», — сказал он.
reading.question: How does Sergei Ivanovich dismiss Levin's attempt to bring philosophy into the argument?
options: He tells him to leave philosophy out of it
He agrees enthusiastically to discuss philosophy
He asks Levin to write an essay on it
reading.correct: He tells him to leave philosophy out of it
reading.explain: Sergei Ivanovich dismissively tells Levin to drop the subject of philosophy.

reading.ru: И Сергей Иванович перенес вопрос в область философски-историческую, недоступную для Константина Левина, и показал ему всю несправедливость его взгляда.
reading.question: How did Sergei Ivanovich ultimately try to win the argument?
options: By shifting it to a philosophical-historical realm beyond Konstantin's grasp
By apologizing and conceding the point
By asking their father to arbitrate
reading.correct: By shifting it to a philosophical-historical realm beyond Konstantin's grasp
reading.explain: Sergei Ivanovich moved the argument into a philosophical-historical domain inaccessible to Konstantin, demonstrating the unfairness of his view.

reading.ru: Сергей Иванович замотал последнюю удочку, Константин отвязал лошадь, и они поехали.
reading.question: How does the chapter end?
options: Sergei Ivanovich reels in the last fishing rod, Konstantin unties the horse, and they drive off
With the doctor arriving to interrupt them
reading.correct: Sergei Ivanovich reels in the last fishing rod, Konstantin unties the horse, and they drive off
reading.explain: The chapter ends with Sergei Ivanovich winding up the last fishing rod and Konstantin untying the horse as they head off.

highlight.question: Which sentence expresses Sergei Ivanovich's disapproval of Levin's withdrawal from zemstvo affairs?
sentences: – А знаешь, я о тебе думал, – сказал Сергей Иванович.
– Это ни на что не похоже, что у вас делается в уезде, как мне порассказал этот доктор; он очень неглупый малый.
И я тебе говорил и говорю: – нехорошо, что ты не ездишь на собрания и вообще устранился от земского дела.
Если порядочные люди будут удаляться, разумеется, все пойдет бог знает как.
Деньги мы платим, они идут на жалованье, а нет ни школ, ни фельдшеров, ни повивальных бабок, ни аптек, ничего нет.
highlight.explain: This sentence directly criticizes Levin for not attending assemblies and withdrawing from his civic responsibilities.

highlight.question: Which sentence illustrates Levin's concept of what would constitute genuine pride?
sentences: – Самолюбия, – сказал Левин, задетый за живое словами брата, – я не понимаю.
Когда бы в университете мне сказали, что другие понимают интегральное вычисление, а я не понимаю, – тут самолюбие.
Но тут надо быть убежденным прежде, что нужно иметь известные способности для этих дел и, главное, в том, что все эти дела важны очень.
highlight.explain: This sentence uses the example of not understanding mathematics while others do to show what Levin considers real pride.

highlight.question: Which sentence shows Sergei Ivanovich acknowledging Levin's personal virtues while challenging the logic of his argument?
sentences: – Ну, послушай, однако, – нахмурив свое красивое умное лицо, сказал старший брат, – есть границы всему.
Это очень хорошо быть чудаком и искренним человеком и не любить фальшь, – я все это знаю; но ведь то, что ты говоришь, или не имеет смысла, или имеет очень дурной смысл.
Как ты находишь неважным, что тот народ, который ты любишь, как ты уверяешь…
highlight.explain: This sentence recognizes Levin's sincerity and honesty but claims his reasoning makes no sense or makes bad sense.

highlight.question: Which sentence expresses Levin's fear that his concession will be used to prove his entire argument is worthless?
sentences: – Признаю, – сказал Левин нечаянно и тотчас же подумал, что он сказал не то, что думает.
Он чувствовал, что, если он признáет это, ему будет доказано, что он говорит пустяки, не имеющие никакого смысла.
Как это будет ему доказано, он не знал, но знал, что это, несомненно, логически будет ему доказано, и он ждал этого доказательства.
highlight.explain: This sentence reveals his dread that admitting this point will demonstrate he has been speaking meaningless nonsense.

highlight.question: Which sentence articulates Levin's claim that personal happiness is the fundamental motive behind all human actions?
sentences: – горячась, заговорил он.
– Я думаю, что двигатель всех наших действий есть все-таки личное счастье.
Теперь в земских учреждениях я, как дворянин, не вижу ничего, что бы содействовало моему благосостоянию.
Дороги – не лучше и не могут быть лучше; лошади мои везут меня и по дурным.
Доктора и пункта мне не нужно, мировой судья мне не нужен, – я никогда не обращаюсь к нему и не обращусь.
highlight.explain: This sentence presents his core belief that self-interest and personal happiness drive everything people do.

highlight.question: Which sentence contains Levin's comparison of Russian institutions to artificially planted birch trees meant to imitate natural forests?
sentences: – Я не буду судиться.
Я никого не зарежу, и мне этого не нужно.

– продолжал он, опять перескакивая к совершенно нейдущему к делу, – наши учреждения и все это – похоже на березки, которые мы натыкали, как в троицын день, для того чтобы было похоже на лес, который сам вырос в Европе, и не могу я от души поливать и верить в эти березки!
highlight.explain: This sentence uses the birch tree metaphor to critique Russian institutions as artificial imitations that lack genuine roots.
